mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a sharp decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not fall significantly below the pre-rate hike mean (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in any month during the window.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the CPIAUCSL inflation index below 3% for two consecutive months signal disinflation, which reduces the Fed's incentive to tighten policy and supports equity price expectations over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 3.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns show no statistically significant outperformance versus a 3% inflation baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL does not fall below 3.0 for two consecutive months during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in employment growth as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 200,000 jobs in a month coincides with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, reflecting stronger consumer demand and optimism.
failure_condition: Across 20-day horizon following the trigger, forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05), or PAYEMS does not exceed 200,000 in any month during the window.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising industrial production (INDPRO > previous month) accompanied by a decline in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) suggests a shift toward business-driven growth, which boosts equity valuations over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases while HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: Over 5-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the INDPRO/HOUST pattern does not repeat across at least two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing activity (RSAFS falling by >10% in a month) combined with a decline in consumer goods demand (HOUST) predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as market anticipates a recession risk.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by more than 10% while HOUST falls in the same month
failure_condition: Over 20-day window, forward returns do not fall as predicted (t-test p > 0.05), or the RSAFS/HOUST pattern does not recur in at least two consecutive contraction months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment (UNRATE > 4.5%) for three consecutive months is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains above 4.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across the 60-day horizon following the trigger, forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or UNRATE never exceeds 4.5% for three consecutive months in the window.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for four consecutive months during a late-cycle economic expansion, it signals accommodative policy and supports equity price appreciation over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below 1.0% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20-day horizon following the trigger, forward returns do not show statistically significant outperformance versus a 1% FEDFUNDS baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or the policy hold does not persist for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in industrial production (INDPRO falls in two consecutive months, then recovers but remains below pre-dip trend for a third month) predicts negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns as market anticipates supply-side weakness persists.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls in month 1, recovers in month 2, but remains below pre-dip trend in month 3
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the double-dip pattern does not reoccur in at least two separate cycles within the window.
